bull.b: Strong demand across data-center interconnect products and LoRa supports durable growth through design wins, expanding deployments, and recurring ecosystem adoption. Backlog and ramps across 800G, 1.6T, and LoRa provide a multi-quarter foundation.

Positive operating and free cash flow despite reported net losses indicates solid cash conversion and internal funding capacity. This supports continued investment in data center and LoRa research while reducing reliance on external capital.

Divesting the cellular module unit can simplify the portfolio and concentrate management, capital, and engineering resources on higher-conviction data-center and LoRa platforms. The transaction may also reduce operational complexity over time.

bear.b: Continued net losses limit retained earnings, shareholder returns, and the company’s ability to absorb execution setbacks. Although gross and operating margins are positive, the gap to sustainable bottom-line profitability remains a fundamental weakness.

The trailing revenue contraction shows that recent growth has not yet translated into consistently expanding annual sales. Dependence on semiconductor cycles, product ramps, and end-market timing could make results uneven over the next several quarters.

Supply constraints can defer shipments and cap near-term revenue capture, while facility integration and ramp costs pressure margins. Meeting demand requires additional capital and execution, creating risks to the expected growth and margin trajectory.
